sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是百分之九十九隐形。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: Ronnie Johnson still remembers the first time he went underground.
sentences.zh: 罗尼·约翰逊依然记得他第一次下井时的情景。

sentences.en: He and a handful of other coal miners piled into a little trailer and descended into the mine.
sentences.zh: 他和另外几名煤矿工人挤进一辆小拖车，一起深入矿井。

sentences.en: We were going down through there hitting bumps and running over little rocks and stuff.
sentences.zh: 我们顺着斜坡往下走，一路上颠簸着，碾过一块块小石头之类的东西。

sentences.en: And I remember laying in that little trailer and the roof was actually so close to me
sentences.zh: 我记得当时自己躺在那辆小拖车里，矿顶离我实在是太近了

sentences.en: that the bib of my hard hat would almost hit the roof.
sentences.zh: 以至于我安全帽的帽檐几乎都要碰到矿顶了。

sentences.en: When they got down to the bottom, Ronnie's boss handed him a wrench
sentences.zh: 当他们到达底部时，罗尼的上司递给他一把扳手

sentences.en: and told him to open a nearby water line.
sentences.zh: 并让他打开附近的一处水管。

sentences.en: But someone had forgotten to cut the water off.
sentences.zh: 但当时有人忘了把总水闸关上。

sentences.en: Like water just started spraying me.
sentences.zh: 水当时直接就朝我喷了过来。

sentences.en: It just sprayed all in my face and all over me.
sentences.zh: 水全喷到我脸上以及我全身各处。

sentences.en: I was soaking wet and I just like fell up against the rib, you know, the wall of coal.
sentences.zh: 我全身湿透了，整个人直接瘫倒在煤壁上，也就是煤炭筑成的墙上。

sentences.en: And I thought to myself, what have I done?
sentences.zh: 当时我心里想，我这都干了些什么？

sentences.en: As a new miner in a dangerous industry,
sentences.zh: 作为一个身处高危行业的矿工新丁，

sentences.en: Ronnie had to go through an intensive orientation process before this first trip underground.
sentences.zh: 罗尼在第一次下井前，必须接受严格的入职培训流程。

sentences.en: That's producer Irina Zhorov.
sentences.zh: 那是制作人伊琳娜·霍罗夫。

sentences.en: Ronnie is actually my partner's father.
sentences.zh: 罗尼其实是我伴侣的父亲。

sentences.en: He lives in northern Alabama and on a recent visit as the family cooked dinner,
sentences.zh: 他住在阿拉巴马州北部，最近有一次家里人正在做晚饭时，

sentences.en: Ronnie and I went out to his workshop where he likes to sit and smoke
sentences.zh: 罗尼和我去了他的工作间，他喜欢坐在那里抽烟，

sentences.en: with only the dogs and cicadas for company.
sentences.zh: 只有几条狗和蝉陪伴着他。

sentences.en: If there's somewhere else you want to do it here or somewhere, I don't care.
sentences.zh: 如果你想去别的地方或者其他地方也行，我都无所谓。

sentences.en: We can just go back there.
sentences.zh: 我们可以直接去那边。

sentences.en: He told me about how he sat through 40 hours of training and safety classes
sentences.zh: 他跟我讲了他如何经历了整整40小时的培训和安全课程，

sentences.en: before going down into the mines.
sentences.zh: 然后才下到矿井里去。

sentences.en: At the end, he was issued a hard hat that identified him as a rookie.
sentences.zh: 培训结束后，他领到了一顶标明他是新人的安全帽。

sentences.en: The hard hat was yellow.
sentences.zh: 那顶安全帽是黄色的。

sentences.en: It was like you stood out from here to the road, you know.
sentences.zh: 那感觉就像是你站在从这儿一直到大马路那么显眼，你懂的。

sentences.en: It was terrible.
sentences.zh: 那可太糟糕了。

sentences.en: It was terrible.
sentences.zh: 那真的太糟糕了。

sentences.en: Was it terrible because you'd get, you'd get like crap from the other men?
sentences.zh: 糟糕是因为你会遭到其他老工人的奚落和捉弄吗？

sentences.en: Oh, yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，对，没错。

sentences.en: Everybody knew you was a rookie, you know, and just, you know, practical jokes.
sentences.zh: 所有人都知道你是个菜鸟，你知道的，然后就会搞一些恶作剧。

sentences.en: Just nothing serious, but.
sentences.zh: 倒也没什么大不了的，不过。

sentences.en: In addition to this terrible yellow hard hat,
sentences.zh: 除了这顶糟糕的黄色安全帽之外，

sentences.en: the safety man at his mine also gave him a sticker.
sentences.zh: 他矿上的安全员还给了他一枚贴纸。

sentences.en: Yeah, it was this sticker right here.
sentences.zh: 对，就是这枚贴纸。

sentences.en: It's a red rhombus about two by two inches with a reflective white center.
sentences.zh: 这是一个大约两英寸见方的红色菱形贴纸，中间带有反光的白色部分。

sentences.en: A-B-C, and it says, always be careful.
sentences.zh: 上面写着A-B-C，意思是“时刻保持小心”。

sentences.en: But A-B-C was a company named Alabama Byproducts Corporation.
sentences.zh: 但A-B-C其实是一家名为阿拉巴马副产品公司的缩写。

sentences.en: Ronnie got a few of these stickers back then.
sentences.zh: 罗尼当时收集了好几张这种贴纸。

sentences.en: He put one in a box and one on his brand new yellow hat.
sentences.zh: 他把一张放进盒子里，另一张贴在了他崭新的黄帽子上。

sentences.en: This was just the beginning of Ronnie's sticker collecting.
sentences.zh: 这只是罗尼收集贴纸生涯的开始。

sentences.en: After 34 years as a miner,
sentences.zh: 在当了34年矿工之后，

sentences.en: he now has several photo albums filled with thousands of stickers.
sentences.zh: 他现在拥有好几本装满了数千张贴纸的照片册。

sentences.en: Some are inside jokes.
sentences.zh: 有些是内部笑话。

sentences.en: Some commemorate big events at work.
sentences.zh: 有些是为了纪念工作中的重大事件。

sentences.en: Lots of other coal miners across the country have collections just like Ronnie's.
sentences.zh: 全国各地的许多其他煤矿工人也都有着像罗尼一样的收藏。

sentences.en: Miners use these stickers for safety and for communication
sentences.zh: 矿工们在矿井里使用这些贴纸是为了安全、为了交流，

sentences.en: and as a kind of currency down in the mines.
sentences.zh: 并且把它们当作矿井底下的一种通用货币。

sentences.en: It was just what coal miners did, you know.
sentences.zh: 这不过是煤矿工人们惯常做的事，你懂的。

sentences.en: Kids collect baseball cars in the coal mines.
sentences.zh: 孩子们收集棒球卡，而在煤矿里，

sentences.en: You know, that's all you had really to collect, you know, was coal mining stickers.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你真正能收集的也就只有煤矿贴纸了。

sentences.en: One of the darkest of all working environments, underground mines.
sentences.zh: 地下矿井是所有工作环境中最为黑暗的地方之一。

sentences.en: Since the beginning of underground mining,
sentences.zh: 自地下采矿诞生以来，

sentences.en: one of the biggest dangers in the workplace has been the darkness.
sentences.zh: 工作场所面临的最大危险之一就是黑暗。

sentences.en: Coal miners of today would shudder at the thought of using some of the early methods of coal mine illumination.
sentences.zh: 如今的煤矿工人只要一想到过去使用过的那些早期煤矿照明方法，就会不寒而栗。

sentences.en: Well into the era of industrial society, miners were still using open flames as their only source of light.
sentences.zh: 直到工业社会高度发达的时期，矿工们依然在使用明火作为唯一的的光源。

sentences.en: The darkness makes accidents more likely.
sentences.zh: 黑暗使得事故更容易发生。

sentences.en: And even though technology has improved to make mines brighter and safer, it's still an issue.
sentences.zh: 尽管技术已经有了进步，使得矿井变得更加明亮和安全，但这仍然是一个问题。

sentences.en: The culture of mining, to a certain degree, has been shaped by the level of risk involved.
sentences.zh: 采矿文化在某种程度上是由其所涉及的风险程度塑造的。

sentences.en: Work cultures have very strong cultures, especially ones that face danger,
sentences.zh: 各行各业的工作文化往往具有很强的特性，特别是那些面对危险的行业，

sentences.en: like mining, firefighting, police work, the military, deep sea fishing, etc.
sentences.zh: 比如采矿、消防、警察工作、军队、深海捕鱼等等。

sentences.en: This is Elaine Cullen.
sentences.zh: 这位是伊莱恩·库伦。

sentences.en: She's an occupational ethnographer and she spent a lot of time with miners,
sentences.zh: 她是一位职业人类学家，花了很多时间与矿工们相处，

sentences.en: like actually down in the mines with them.
sentences.zh: 甚至真的和他们一起下到矿井底下。

sentences.en: Mining has a very strong culture.
sentences.zh: 采矿业有着非常强烈的文化氛围。

sentences.en: I think the reason is because people who work underground are well aware of the fact that
sentences.zh: 我认为原因在于，在地下工作的人们都非常清楚这样一个事实：

sentences.en: every day you go in, you don't know if you're coming out.
sentences.zh: 你每天进去，都不知道自己能不能活着出来。

sentences.en: The first time Cullen went down into a mine,
sentences.zh: 库伦第一次下到矿井时，

sentences.en: she was told that she had to have something reflective on her hard hat.
sentences.zh: 有人告诉她，她的安全帽上必须贴有反光材质的东西。

sentences.en: There's a lot of heavy machinery moving around,
sentences.zh: 那里有很多重型机械在移动，

sentences.en: from buses to the shears, roof bolters, and other tools used to extract coal.
sentences.zh: 从运载车到采煤机、顶板锚杆机以及用于开采煤炭的其他工具。

sentences.en: People get hit.
sentences.zh: 人们会被撞到。

sentences.en: They get run over.
sentences.zh: 他们会被碾压。

sentences.en: They get crushed by mobile equipment.
sentences.zh: 他们会被移动设备压扁。

sentences.en: And so, reflective material increases the visibility of the people underground.
sentences.zh: 因此，反光材料能够提高地下人员的能见度。

sentences.en: We put strips of reflective tape on the back of our hard hats,
sentences.zh: 我们在安全帽的背面贴上了反光胶带条，

sentences.en: but then it became pretty obvious that other people had other things on their hard hats,
sentences.zh: 但随后大家很明显地发现，其他人的安全帽上还有别的东西，

sentences.en: and these were stickers.
sentences.zh: 那就是贴纸。

sentences.en: The stickers had originally been little advertisements that the manufacturers of mining equipment handed out.
sentences.zh: 这些贴纸最初是采矿设备制造商派发的小广告。

sentences.en: Even before the late 1960s, when mining safety laws started requiring reflective materials underground,
sentences.zh: 早在20世纪60年代末采矿安全法律开始强制要求井下使用反光材料之前，

sentences.en: miners used those stickers to stay visible to each other.
sentences.zh: 矿工们就已经在利用这些贴纸来确保彼此能够被看见了。

sentences.en: But as time passed, the stickers evolved.
sentences.zh: 但随着时间推移，这些贴纸不断演变。

sentences.en: They became more personal and started to tell miners' stories.
sentences.zh: 它们变得更加个性化，开始讲述矿工们自己的故事。

sentences.en: And the mine companies themselves started printing stickers for their workers.
sentences.zh: 矿业公司本身也开始为员工印制贴纸。

sentences.en: They went from simple ads to signaling an identity.
sentences.zh: 它们从简单的广告变成了彰显身份的标志。

sentences.en: These are sort of, they're symbols, symbols of the mining industry, and that you're part of it, that you're a miner.
sentences.zh: 这些东西有点像是采矿业的象征，是采矿业的符号，表明你是其中的一部分，你是一名矿工。

sentences.en: After a year in the Alabama mine, Ronnie swapped out his yellow hard hat for a black one,
sentences.zh: 在阿拉巴马的矿井里干了一年后，罗尼把他的黄色安全帽换成了一顶黑色的，

sentences.en: which meant he was no longer a rookie.
sentences.zh: 这意味着他不再是个菜鸟了。

sentences.en: With that came more stickers.
sentences.zh: 随之而来的是更多的贴纸。

sentences.en: The stickers always came in twos.
sentences.zh: 这些贴纸总是成双成对地出现。

sentences.en: One went on his hard hat, which he actually brought out to show me.
sentences.zh: 一张贴在他的安全帽上，他实际上把帽子拿出来给我看了。

sentences.en: So where's your six inches of reflective tape?
sentences.zh: 那你的六英寸反光胶带去哪了？

sentences.en: I probably covered all mine up with stickers.
sentences.zh: 我大概全用贴纸给盖住了吧。

sentences.en: You can see all the Alabama stickers on it, you know.
sentences.zh: 你看上面所有的阿拉巴马贴纸，你就明白了。

sentences.en: The other sticker he saved for his growing collection.
sentences.zh: 另一张贴纸则被他存起来，丰富他日益庞大的收藏。

sentences.en: A miner showed Ronnie how to keep the stickers organized,
sentences.zh: 曾有一位老矿工教给罗尼如何将这些贴纸归类整理，

sentences.en: so each week he'd sit down and put the new stickers in an album.
sentences.zh: 于是他每周都会坐下来，把新收到的贴纸放进相册里。

sentences.en: What's this one?
sentences.zh: 这个是什么？

sentences.en: That's the Grim Reaper, it looks like, don't it?
sentences.zh: 这看起来像是个死神，对吧？

sentences.en: It says UMWA.
sentences.zh: 上面写着UMWA。

sentences.en: That's a Union sticker.
sentences.zh: 这是一个工会贴纸。

sentences.en: I'm sure it's got something to do with Black Long.
sentences.zh: 我敢肯定这跟Black Long有关。

sentences.en: Managers and the safety man at his mine gave him stickers with the mine name on them,
sentences.zh: 他矿上的经理和安全员会送给他印有矿名字样的贴纸，

sentences.en: and his union gave him stickers with union messages on them.
sentences.zh: 而工会则会送给他印有工会口号的贴纸。

sentences.en: One of his favorite stickers has the state of Alabama outlined in red,
sentences.zh: 他最喜欢的贴纸之一上面描绘了阿拉巴马州的红色轮廓，

sentences.en: and inside it says, Alabama Coal Miner.
sentences.zh: 里面写着“阿拉巴马煤矿工”。

sentences.en: That's kind of a pride thing there, you know, Alabama Coal Miner.
sentences.zh: 这带有一种自豪感，你知道的，阿拉巴马煤矿工。

sentences.en: As he gained more experience, he got stickers commemorating his accomplishments.
sentences.zh: 随着经验越来越丰富，他得到了能够纪念自己成就的贴纸。

sentences.en: He worked at a company early on that counted the amount of coal mined
sentences.zh: 他早期曾在一个公司工作，那里的煤炭开采量是根据

sentences.en: by the number of cars filled during a shift.
sentences.zh: 一个班次中装满的矿车数量来计算的。

sentences.en: Something like 100 cars was okay.
sentences.zh: 类似装满100车就算合格。

sentences.en: But Ronnie has a sticker that says his team mined 150 cars in one shift.
sentences.zh: 但罗尼有一张贴纸，上面显示他们团队在一个班次里开采了150车。

sentences.en: And in this sticker it says 150 Car Club with a little Playboy Bunny on there.
sentences.zh: 在这张贴纸上写着“150车俱乐部”，上面还有一个小花花公子兔的标志。

sentences.en: He also has one commemorating 225 cars in a shift, which is a big deal.
sentences.zh: 他还有一张纪念单班开采225车的贴纸，这可是一件大事。

sentences.en: You're going to have a big run, then the next night you're outside,
sentences.zh: 当你经历了一次产量大爆发，然后第二天晚上你在井外，

sentences.en: and all the guys that didn't have such a good run or whatever,
sentences.zh: 所有那些产量不太好或者诸如此类的小伙子们都在那儿，

sentences.en: and your boss is going around giving you these stickers.
sentences.zh: 而你的老板正四处给你发这些贴纸。

sentences.en: And it was just kind of an incentive thing.
sentences.zh: 这其实算是一种激励机制。

sentences.en: In the 1960s and 70s, a number of major mine safety laws were passed in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪60、70年代，美国通过了一系列重大的矿山安全法规。

sentences.en: And Elaine Cullen started working at a new agency that was responsible for studying
sentences.zh: 伊莱恩·库伦开始在一个新机构工作，该机构负责研究

sentences.en: and enforcing safety in the mines.
sentences.zh: 并推行矿山安全标准。

sentences.en: For years, she researched mining culture.
sentences.zh: 多年来，她一直在研究采矿文化。

sentences.en: In the 2000s, the National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health,
sentences.zh: 20世纪2000年代，国家职业安全卫生研究所，

sentences.en: a federal agency, hired her to develop a safety training program for coal miners.
sentences.zh: 一个联邦机构，雇佣她来为煤矿工人开发安全培训项目。

sentences.en: By that time, she knew who she was dealing with.
sentences.zh: 到那时，她已经知道自己要面对的是什么人了。

sentences.en: So she knew she might be facing some skepticism from the miners she was trying to reach.
sentences.zh: 所以她清楚，她可能会面临来自那些她试图接触的矿工们的怀疑态度。

sentences.en: I don't look like a miner.
sentences.zh: 我看起来一点也不像个矿工。

sentences.en: I'm a woman, and most of them are not.
sentences.zh: 我是个女性，而他们大多不是。

sentences.en: So getting them to work with me,
sentences.zh: 所以要让他们愿意跟我合作，

sentences.en: especially when I was a representative of the federal government,
sentences.zh: 特别是当我代表联邦政府的时候，

sentences.en: and, you know, they are a little leery to, you know, work with the government.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，他们对跟政府打交道多少有点戒备。

sentences.en: But Elaine had seen that the miners were really into these stickers.
sentences.zh: 但伊莱恩发现矿工们对这些贴纸非常热衷。

sentences.en: And she figured she could use them to gain their trust and to convey messages about safety.
sentences.zh: 她琢磨着可以利用这些贴纸来赢得他们的信任，并传达有关安全的讯息。

sentences.en: But she knew just putting work safe on a sticker wouldn't cut it.
sentences.zh: 但她深知，仅在贴纸上写个“注意安全”是远远不够的。

sentences.en: She needed something to grab the miners' attention.
sentences.zh: 她需要一些能够抓住矿工们眼球的东西。

sentences.en: I mean, we were working out in eastern Kentucky.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们当时在肯塔基州东部工作。

sentences.en: It was a mining community with deep cultural ties to coal.
sentences.zh: 那是一个与煤炭有着深厚文化纽带的采矿社区。

sentences.en: And she started to notice something.
sentences.zh: 接着她开始注意到一件事。

sentences.en: She'd be walking along with the safety guy.
sentences.zh: 她会和安全员一起散步。

sentences.en: And as we would approach another miner, he would squeal like a pig.
sentences.zh: 每当他们接近另一个矿工时，那个人就会像猪一样尖叫起来。

sentences.en: I finally asked him, I said, Jesse, what's going on here?
sentences.zh: 我最后忍不住问他，我说，杰西，这到底是怎么回事？

sentences.en: Why are they doing that?
sentences.zh: 他们为什么要那样叫？

sentences.en: And he said, oh, they're just saying they know I'm a coal hog.
sentences.zh: 他说，哦，他们只是在说他们知道我是个“煤炭狂”。

sentences.en: And I said, what is a coal hog?
sentences.zh: 我说，什么是“煤炭狂”？

sentences.en: And he said, coal hog is hungry for coal, greedy for coal, can't ever get enough.
sentences.zh: 他说，煤炭狂就是渴望煤炭、贪婪煤炭、永远也挖不够的人。

sentences.en: Meaning that you're a good miner.
sentences.zh: 意思就是说你是个优秀的矿工。

sentences.en: So Elaine took the idea and designed a sticker with a big muscular pig with a hard hat on.
sentences.zh: 于是伊莱恩采用了这个创意，设计了一款贴纸，上面是一头戴着安全帽、肌肉发达的大肥猪。

sentences.en: And it says, coal hogs work safe.
sentences.zh: 上面写着：“煤炭狂安全作业。”

sentences.en: So what we were doing is putting those two ideas together.
sentences.zh: 所以我们所做的，就是把这两个想法结合起来。

sentences.en: That you can be a coal hog, but you can also work safely.
sentences.zh: 你可以是个煤矿老手，但也可以安全地工作。

sentences.en: The miners loved it.
sentences.zh: 矿工们很喜欢这个。

sentences.en: Oh, gosh, I think we printed 3,000 to begin with.
sentences.zh: 哦天哪，我想我们一开始印了大约3000张。

sentences.en: And I have one little packet left that I'm kind of keeping as a, you know, keepsake.
sentences.zh: 我这里还剩一个小册子，我留着当个纪念品什么的。

sentences.en: Some of Cullen's other designs were duds.
sentences.zh: 卡伦的其他一些设计并不成功。

sentences.en: Her team made one with a dead canary.
sentences.zh: 她的团队设计了一款带着死金丝雀的贴纸。

sentences.en: Canaries were once used to check for bad air in a mine.
sentences.zh: 金丝雀过去常被用来检查矿井里是否有毒气。

sentences.en: But that was a long time ago.
sentences.zh: 但这已经是很久以前的事了。

sentences.en: And the younger miners didn't get it.
sentences.zh: 年轻的矿工们并不理解。

sentences.en: Other stickers catering to the raunchy humor in the mines didn't pass muster with her bosses in the federal government.
sentences.zh: 其他迎合矿井粗俗幽默的贴纸也没有通过她联邦政府上司的审查。

sentences.en: For example, they designed one sticker to remind miners to check for gas in the mines.
sentences.zh: 例如，他们设计了一款贴纸，提醒矿工检查矿井中的瓦斯。

sentences.en: So what the, this one was at the back end of a donkey and had the donkey kind of looking back at you.
sentences.zh: 这个设计是一只驴子的后半身，驴子还回头看着你。

sentences.en: And it said, don't be an ass, check for gas.
sentences.zh: 上面写着：别当个大傻瓜，检查瓦斯。

sentences.en: And kind of had this little cloud coming out.
sentences.zh: 旁边还画了一小团冒出来的气体。

sentences.en: Gas can be really dangerous underground.
sentences.zh: 地下瓦斯可能会非常危险。

sentences.en: And donkeys were once used to carry coal out of the mines.
sentences.zh: 而且驴子过去曾被用来把煤炭从矿井里运出来。

sentences.en: Oh boy, the, the, uh, folks in Washington didn't like that one.
sentences.zh: 天哪，华盛顿的那些官员们可不喜欢这个。

sentences.en: But the miners loved it.
sentences.zh: 但矿工们非常喜欢。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Unless Elaine visited your mine, it'd be hard to get one of these stickers.
sentences.zh: 除非伊莱恩去过你们的矿井，否则很难弄到这些贴纸。

sentences.en: A lot of the stickers were specialized or localized depending on what organization or company designed them.
sentences.zh: 很多贴纸都是专门定制的，或者根据设计它们的组织或公司而具有地方特色。

sentences.en: That's part of what made collecting them fun.
sentences.zh: 这也是收集它们充满乐趣的一部分原因。

sentences.en: I have over 26,000 different stickers in my collection.
sentences.zh: 我的收藏里有超过26,000张不同的贴纸。

sentences.en: And I've, I've kind of come to believe that you either are a collector or you're not.
sentences.zh: 我渐渐开始相信，一个人要么是个收藏家，要么就不是。

sentences.en: And if you're not a collector, you just don't get it.
sentences.zh: 如果你不是收藏家，你根本不会懂。

sentences.en: And if you are a collector, you just really can't help yourself.
sentences.zh: 而如果你是个收藏家，你真的会情不自禁。

sentences.en: This is Lenny Hanner.
sentences.zh: 这是兰尼·汉纳。

sentences.en: And I'm a coal miner from Southern Illinois.
sentences.zh: 我是一名来自伊利诺伊州南部的煤矿工人。

sentences.en: Lenny has worked in coal mines for 40 years.
sentences.zh: 兰尼在煤矿工作了40年。

sentences.en: He's a major sticker collector.
sentences.zh: 他是一个资深的贴纸收藏家。

sentences.en: At the height of his collecting in the 1980s,
sentences.zh: 在20世纪80年代他收藏的鼎盛时期，

sentences.en: he'd exchange stickers with other collectors across the country
sentences.zh: 他会与全国各地的其他收藏家交换贴纸，

sentences.en: and go to sticker swaps almost every weekend.
sentences.zh: 几乎每个周末都去参加贴纸交换会。

sentences.en: Those are meetups where miners exchange pieces.
sentences.zh: 那是矿工们交换藏品的聚会。

sentences.en: Lenny says unique stickers were like currency in the mines,
sentences.zh: 兰尼说，独一无二的贴纸就像是矿井里的流通货币，

sentences.en: a way to buy or sell favors and help.
sentences.zh: 是买卖人情和寻求帮助的一种方式。

sentences.en: For instance, say you're a trucker and you've rolled up to the mines with a big load of supplies.
sentences.zh: 比方说，你是一个卡车司机，运送着一大车物资来到了矿井。

sentences.en: You ask some of the miners to help you unload.
sentences.zh: 你请一些矿工帮你卸货。

sentences.en: The first thing they wanted to know is, do you have any stickers?
sentences.zh: 他们问的第一件事就是：你有贴纸吗？

sentences.en: Without stickers, the miners wouldn't exactly rush to help.
sentences.zh: 如果没有贴纸，矿工们可不会那么积极地来帮忙。

sentences.en: So, they all learned that they had stickers in that truck when they arrived.
sentences.zh: 所以，当他们到达时，大家都知道那辆卡车里有贴纸。

sentences.en: And they tend to get unloaded a whole lot faster that way.
sentences.zh: 用这种方法，卸货的速度往往会快得多。

sentences.en: Lenny still works for a mining company, but above ground these days.
sentences.zh: 兰尼现在仍然为一家矿业公司工作，不过如今是在地面上。

sentences.en: He lives in an old mining town in a house that was once owned by a mining company.
sentences.zh: 他住在一个老矿区的一栋房子里，这栋房子曾经属于一家矿业公司。

sentences.en: And he's got a full room devoted to mining memorabilia.
sentences.zh: 他有一个专门用来存放采矿纪念品的房间。

sentences.en: I'm married to the, you know, the most understanding woman in the world.
sentences.zh: 我娶了世界上最通情达理的妻子。

sentences.en: He keeps his stickers in 27 albums organized by type of sticker.
sentences.zh: 他把贴纸保存在27本按贴纸类型分类的相册里。

sentences.en: The ones printed by mining companies, the ones equipment manufacturers gave out,
sentences.zh: 有矿业公司印刷的，有设备制造商发放的，

sentences.en: the ones focused on safety and union issues.
sentences.zh: 还有专注于安全和工会问题的。

sentences.en: Some of them are especially sentimental.
sentences.zh: 其中一些格外具有纪念意义。

sentences.en: I have a sticker that I got from a friend of mine, and he recently passed away.
sentences.zh: 我有一张贴纸是一个朋友送给我的，他最近去世了。

sentences.en: And I have just a couple stickers in my collection that really make me think of him when I see them.
sentences.zh: 我的收藏里只有几张贴纸，每当我看到它们，就会深深地想起他。

sentences.en: The sticker albums function just like photo albums, reminding miners of their milestones and stories.
sentences.zh: 这些贴纸相册就像相册一样，提醒着矿工们的里程碑和故事。

sentences.en: They are just little pieces of our history, of our past, little mementos.
sentences.zh: 它们只是我们历史、我们过去的小片断，小纪念品。

sentences.en: I guess maybe like a postcard if you travel, that you might pick up a postcard that reminds you of something from the paSt.
sentences.zh: 我想也许就像你旅行时买的明信片一样，你可能会挑一张能让你想起过去某事的明信片。

sentences.en: We can just see our past mining history there on the pages of the album.
sentences.zh: 我们可以在相册的页面上看到我们过去的采矿历史。

sentences.en: Of course, just like with photos, some of the darker memories don't end up in the album.
sentences.zh: 当然，就像照片一样，一些黑暗的记忆并没有进入相册。

sentences.en: In 2011, after more than 30 years in the mines, my partner's dad, Ronnie, had an accident.
sentences.zh: 2011年，在矿井工作了30多年后，我伴侣的父亲罗尼发生了一场事故。

sentences.en: We were living a thousand miles away and paced around in my living room as news trickled in.
sentences.zh: 我们当时住在千里之外，随着消息一点点传进来，我在客厅里急得踱来踱去。

sentences.en: We eventually learned that his hand got pulled into a machine, and it took a finger.
sentences.zh: 我们最终得知他的手被卷进了一台机器里，断了一根手指。

sentences.en: Down in Alabama, he was rushed to a hospital.
sentences.zh: 在阿拉巴马州，他被紧急送往医院。

sentences.en: He was told to call his wife, Debra.
sentences.zh: 他被告知给他的妻子黛布拉打电话。

sentences.en: At first, he didn't want to call.
sentences.zh: 起初，他不想打。

sentences.en: What happened in the mine stayed in the mine.
sentences.zh: 矿里发生的事就留在矿里。

sentences.en: But the nurse insisted, and Debra happened to be nearby.
sentences.zh: 但护士坚持要打，而黛布拉正好在附近。

sentences.en: I remember Debra looking at me when she came in the room and said,
sentences.zh: 我记得黛布拉进房间时看着我说：

sentences.en: Ronnie, Johnson, how did you get so dirty?
sentences.zh: 罗尼·约翰逊，你怎么弄得这么脏？

sentences.en: You know, like, I mean, I'd been getting that wife for years, and I guess she never saw me.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我的意思是，我已经听我老婆这么唠叨多年了，我想她大概从没真正看清过我。

sentences.en: I had on my rubber boots, and my face was all black, and my hand was all wrapped up in a bandage.
sentences.zh: 我穿着胶靴，脸全黑了，手也被厚厚的绷带包着。

sentences.en: He'd never really shared much about his life in the mine with his family.
sentences.zh: 他从未真正向家人分享过他在矿里的生活。

sentences.en: I guess they had never saw me like that.
sentences.zh: 我想他们以前从没见过我那个样子。

sentences.en: I didn't tell them what I went through.
sentences.zh: 我没有告诉他们我经历了什么。

sentences.en: The sticker albums stacked up in his cozy house only tell their stories to those who know how to read them.
sentences.zh: 他那舒适的房子里堆得高高的贴纸相册，只有懂得如何阅读的人才能听懂它们的故事。

sentences.en: Ronnie says before he lost his finger, he'd gone 31 years without spending a night in the hospital.
sentences.zh: 罗尼说，在失去手指之前，他已经连续31年没有在医院过夜了。

sentences.en: He'd never ridden in an ambulance and never had an accident in the mine that made him lose work hours.
sentences.zh: 他从未坐过救护车，在矿里也从未发生过导致他耽误工作时间的事故。

sentences.en: I caught up for all those 31 years in one night, though, you know.
sentences.zh: 不过，我把那31年没受过的罪在短短一夜之间全补回来了。

sentences.en: Ronnie never got a sticker for that.
sentences.zh: 罗尼可没有因此得到一张贴纸。

sentences.en: So what do you do with a mine that's no longer productive?
sentences.zh: 那么，对于一处不再产出资源的矿井，你该怎么处理呢？

sentences.en: Lots of things, it turns out.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，有很多方法。

sentences.en: Kurt Kolstad tells us about his favorite examples of adaptive reuse after this.
sentences.zh: 接下来，库尔特·科尔斯特德将为我们介绍他最喜欢的适应性再利用案例。

sentences.en: We were attracted to the coal miner stickers because it was this cool way that design and the culture of mining intersected,
sentences.zh: 我们被煤矿工人的贴纸所吸引，因为这是设计与采矿文化交织的一种酷炫方式，

sentences.en: and it brought to mind another interesting juxtaposition of design and abandoned mines that Kurt Kolstad wrote about on the website.
sentences.zh: 这也让人联想到了库尔特·科尔斯特德在网站上写过关于设计与废弃矿井的另一个有趣结合。

sentences.en: So I asked him to come in the studio and talk about it.
sentences.zh: 所以我请他来到演播室谈论这个话题。

sentences.en: I think a lot of people tend to have this idea that mines are these, you know, rickety, dangerous places to go,
sentences.zh: 我想很多人往往会有这样一种印象，认为矿井是那种摇摇晃晃、充满危险的地方，

sentences.en: you know, with rotting timber frames holding up sections of tunnel that could collapse on you at any moment.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，靠着腐烂的木框支撑着随时可能坍塌的隧道部分。

sentences.en: But the reality is a lot of mines are much bigger than that and much more stable than that and really have promising futures doing much different things than they were designed for.
sentences.zh: 但现实是，许多矿井比这大得多，也稳固得多，并且有着广阔的前景，可以用来做很多与它们最初设计完全不同的事情。

sentences.en: What's a good example?
sentences.zh: 有什么好例子吗？

sentences.en: So one example would be there's this really cool mine in Romania that was actually first mined for salt nearly a thousand years ago,
sentences.zh: 一个例子是罗马尼亚有一个非常酷的矿井，大约在一千年前它最初是一座盐矿，

sentences.en: and it's been used on and off as a salt mine ever since.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，它断断续续一直被用作盐矿。

sentences.en: So it's really deep and it's really complex.
sentences.zh: 所以它非常深，结构也非常复杂。

sentences.en: And recently they decided we're going to turn this into an attraction.
sentences.zh: 最近他们决定把它变成一个旅游景点。

sentences.en: So they made it a museum.
sentences.zh: 于是他们把它改造成了一个博物馆。

sentences.en: They made it kind of a theme park.
sentences.zh: 他们把它弄得有点像个主题公园。

sentences.en: You can go down there and, like, boat around on this water.
sentences.zh: 你可以到底下去，比如在这片水面上划船。

sentences.en: And the pictures are just sort of mesmerizing.
sentences.zh: 那些照片简直令人着迷。

sentences.en: They've really lit this place up.
sentences.zh: 他们把这个地方点缀得灯火辉煌。

sentences.en: So you can go down and really get a sense of the geology but also just have this kind of fun experience underground.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以下去真正领略地质奇观，同时还能获得这种地下趣味体验。

sentences.en: Cool.
sentences.zh: 太酷了。

sentences.en: Are there any in the U.S.?
sentences.zh: 美国有这样的地方吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 有的。

sentences.en: In Kansas, there's a data center.
sentences.zh: 堪萨斯州有一个数据中心。

sentences.en: It's a little less exciting but a little more functional on a sort of day-to-day basis that essentially uses the natural, you know,
sentences.zh: 它没那么刺激，但在日常运作中更具实用性，它基本上利用了天然的，你知道的，

sentences.en: even temperatures and the protection of this mine space, this old limestone mine space,
sentences.zh: 恒定的温度以及这个矿区空间（旧石灰石矿区空间）的保护作用，

sentences.en: to house its servers.
sentences.zh: 来容纳他们的服务器。

sentences.en: And you can imagine, you know, if you're just trying to keep these servers running, you know,
sentences.zh: 你可以想象，如果你只是想让这些服务器保持运行，你知道的，

sentences.en: during any kind of weather, the perfect place is just to tuck them on it around.
sentences.zh: 在任何天气下，最完美的地方就是把它们安顿在这里。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, that makes a ton of sense to me.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这对我来说太合情合理了。

sentences.en: And there's also a research facility that is doing experiments on dark matter far underground in South Dakota in an old gold mine.
sentences.zh: 南达科他州的一个旧金矿地下深处，还有一个研究设施正在做暗物质实验。

sentences.en: It's about a mile deep.
sentences.zh: 它大约有一英里深。

sentences.en: And it turns out that there's a lot of particles that sort of just float through space and bombard our atmosphere on a pretty regular basis.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，有很多粒子在太空中漂浮，并以相当高的频率轰击我们的大气层。

sentences.en: And getting below the surface, they can get away from a lot of that noise and have a lot more of a kind of clean experiment.
sentences.zh: 通过深入地下，他们可以避开许多这种干扰，从而进行更加纯净的实验。

sentences.en: Yeah, totally.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Oh, that makes a ton of sense.
sentences.zh: 哦，这太有道理了。

sentences.en: Oh, that's so cool.
sentences.zh: 哦，太酷了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And, you know, if they decide to destroy the universe, at least they're a mile underground.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，如果他们决定毁灭宇宙，至少他们是在地下深处一英里处。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, yeah, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，没错吧？

sentences.en: The hope is that they'd only just destroy their lab in a mountain or something, right?
sentences.zh: 希望他们只是摧毁了山里的实验室什么的，对吧？

sentences.en: Well, there you go.
sentences.zh: 好吧，就是这样。

sentences.en: So what's your favorite example?
sentences.zh: 那你最喜欢哪个例子？

sentences.en: So my favorite is probably the Louisville Mega Cavern, which is this huge, huge underground space in Louisville, Kentucky.
sentences.zh: 我最喜欢的可能是路易斯维尔超级溶洞，这是肯塔基州路易斯维尔一个非常巨大的地下空间。

sentences.en: If you buy the argument that it's now a building, it's the largest building in Kentucky at about four million square feet.
sentences.zh: 如果你承认它现在是一座建筑物的话，它大约有四百万平方英尺，是肯塔基州最大的建筑物。

sentences.en: And basically, this mine opened in the 1930s.
sentences.zh: 基本上，这个矿井开放于20世纪30年代。

sentences.en: They dug out limestone for decades, really carved this thing out.
sentences.zh: 几十年来他们一直在开采石灰石，真正把这个地方掏空了。

sentences.en: In the 1960s, they actually talked about using it as a fallout shelter in case the Cuban Missile Crisis went the wrong way.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪60年代，他们甚至讨论过万一古巴导弹危机恶化，把它用作防空洞。

sentences.en: And they were planning to pack like tens of thousands of people in there.
sentences.zh: 他们当时计划往里面塞几万名民众。

sentences.en: And then eventually, it sort of fell into disuse.
sentences.zh: 后来它逐渐荒废了。

sentences.en: And some investors came along and said, hey, we could do something with this.
sentences.zh: 接着一些投资者出现了，说，嘿，我们可以用这个做点什么。

sentences.en: And they did.
sentences.zh: 他们确实做到了。

sentences.en: Basically, they bought this thing.
sentences.zh: 基本上，他们买下了这个地方。

sentences.en: And they started, you know, putting businesses in there.
sentences.zh: 然后他们开始，你知道的，把各种企业搬进里面。

sentences.en: They started using it for storage because it's sort of, you know, temperature stable.
sentences.zh: 他们开始用它来做仓储，因为这里你知道的，温度恒定。

sentences.en: It's a good place for storage.
sentences.zh: 这是个存放东西的好地方。

sentences.en: And then they did something kind of weird.
sentences.zh: 然后他们做了一件有点奇怪的事。

sentences.en: And they started adding all these kind of theme park elements to it.
sentences.zh: 他们开始在里面增加各种主题公园的元素。

sentences.en: So you can go take tram tours of the underground.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以去参加地下的电车游览。

sentences.en: You can go take zipline tours.
sentences.zh: 你可以去玩高空滑索。

sentences.en: There's a ropes course.
sentences.zh: 那里还有绳索攀爬课程。

sentences.en: At the heart of it all, one of the biggest functions is this huge, huge 300,000 plus square foot bike park.
sentences.zh: 核心功能之一是一个巨大无比、面积超过30万平方英尺的自行车公园。

sentences.en: And it's like a BMX bike park with like hills and jumps and all that stuff.
sentences.zh: 它就像一个BMX小轮车公园，有山丘、跳台和所有这些设施。

sentences.en: And they build those out of all the sort of fill that was already carved out and sort of laying around from the miners, right?
sentences.zh: 它们是用矿工们原本开采出来并堆放在那里的所有回填土建成的，对吧？

sentences.en: So all they have to do is just kind of pick up the dirt here, shovel it over there, and they can make entirely new courses.
sentences.zh: 所以他们只需要把这里的泥土铲起来，移到那边，就能建造全新的赛道。

sentences.en: Oh, that's so cool.
sentences.zh: 哦，太酷了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And we have some pictures of these on our website.
sentences.zh: 我们的网站上有这些地方的一些照片。

sentences.en: Yeah, we've got a bunch of pictures and some video of this on the website.

sentences.en: 99% Invisible was produced this week by Irina Juroff with Delaney Hall.
sentences.zh: 本周的《99% Invisible》由伊琳娜·尤罗夫（Irina Juroff）和德兰妮·霍尔（Delaney Hall）制作。

sentences.en: Tech production and mix by Sharif Yusuf.
sentences.zh: 技术制作与混音由谢里夫·优素福（Sharif Yusuf）负责。

sentences.en: Music by Sean Rial.
sentences.zh: 音乐由肖恩·里亚尔（Sean Rial）创作。

sentences.en: Our senior editor is Katie Mingle.
sentences.zh: 我们的资深编辑是凯蒂·明格尔（Katie Mingle）。

sentences.en: Kurt Kolstad is the digital director.
sentences.zh: 柯特·科尔斯塔德（Kurt Kolstad）是数字总监。

sentences.en: The rest of the staff is Avery Truffleman, Emmett Fitzgerald, Taryn Mazza, and me, Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 其余的工作人员有艾弗里·特鲁夫曼（Avery Truffleman）、埃米特·菲茨杰拉德（Emmett Fitzgerald）、泰琳·马扎（Taryn Mazza），还有我，罗曼·马尔斯（Roman Mars）。

sentences.en: We are a project of Radiotopia and 91.7 KALW San Francisco and produced on Radio Row in beautiful downtown Oakland, California.
sentences.zh: 我们是 Radiotopia 和旧金山 KALW 91.7 电台的合作项目，在美丽的加利福尼亚州奥克兰市中心无线电街（Radio Row）制作。

sentences.en: You can find 99% Invisible and join discussions about the show on Facebook.
sentences.zh: 您可以在 Facebook 上找到《99% Invisible》并参与节目的讨论。

sentences.en: You can tweet at me at Roman Mars and the show at 99pi.org.
sentences.zh: 您可以在 Twitter 上@我（Roman Mars），或者@节目官方账号（99pi.org）。

sentences.en: We're on Instagram, Tumblr, and Reddit, too.
sentences.zh: 我们也在 Instagram、Tumblr 和 Reddit 上。

sentences.en: But our beautiful home on the internet, with more design stories than we could ever tell you inside this podcast, is our website, 99pi.org.
sentences.zh: 但我们在互联网上美丽的家——这里有我们在本播客中讲不完的设计故事——是我们的网站 99pi.org。

sentences.en: Radiotopia.
sentences.zh: Radiotopia。
